entry_fields.id: stable slug; prose and pin comments cite this, never the number
entry_fields.claim: one sentence, stated the way the book would state it
entry_fields.value: number, [low, high] range, or structured object
entry_fields.source: title / venue / year / locator (doi or url); for papers, the PINNED version
entry_fields.retrieved: ISO date the value was last checked against the source
entry_fields.method: how the value was obtained: quoted, derived, fetched-by-script
entry_fields.fetch: script under registry/fetch/ that can refresh this value, or null for pinned papers
entry_fields.notes: caveats that must travel with the number

claims.claim: During Jharkhand's biometric-authentication reforms, 1.5–2 million legitimate beneficiaries lost access to benefits at some point.
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar, "Identity Verification Standards in Welfare Programs: Experimental Evidence from India", Review of Economics and Statistics 107(2): 372–392 (2025), doi:10.1162/rest_a_01296
claims.notes: Supersedes NBER WP 26744; the WP-era '~2 million' and the spliced 10%/10.6% quotation are corrected in final-research.md (commit 1bcacc7).

claims.claim: In the reconciliation phase, roughly 1.7 million people did not receive PDS benefits in the first month (July 2017).
claims.notes: ~1.2 million under the paper's conservative assumption. The widely quoted '13%' is a percentage-POINT increase in non-receipt in treated blocks, not a share of all beneficiaries.

claims.claim: 88% of cancelled ration cards sampled in the study districts belonged to genuine households.
claims.method: quoted; authors label the figure 'purely descriptive' (non-causal)
claims.notes: Covers the 1.44 lakh cancellations in the 10 study districts — never to be narrated as the Drèze survey's 11 lakh statewide figure.

claims.claim: 11 lakh (1.1 million) ration cards were cancelled in Jharkhand for not being linked to Aadhaar.
claims.source: Drèze, Khalid, Khera & Somanchi, "Aadhaar and Food Security in Jharkhand", Economic and Political Weekly 52(50): 50–60 (16 December 2017)
claims.notes: Statewide administrative figure; distinct population from the study-district sample behind muralidharan-2025-genuine-cards.

claims.claim: US permanent-supportive-housing (Housing First) programs show a median benefit-to-cost ratio of 1.8:1.
claims.source: Jacob et al., "Permanent Supportive Housing With Housing First: Findings From a Community Guide Systematic Economic Review", American Journal of Preventive Medicine (2022)
claims.method: quoted (median across studies; median benefit $18,247/person/year vs median cost $16,479)
claims.notes: Corrects the 'Chapman et al. 2021 / 1.44' citation that stood in final-research.md until commit 74920cd.

claims.claim: Housing First produced a median 88% greater decrease in homelessness and a median 41% greater housing stability than Treatment First or usual care.
claims.source: CPSTF effectiveness review, 26 studies, search through February 2018 (thecommunityguide.org, Housing First finding page)
claims.notes: 88% figure rests on 5 studies, 41% on 13. Never merge into an '88% vs 47%' comparison — that garble stood until commit 74920cd.

claims.claim: Over 44,000 separate collateral consequences exist in US federal and state law and regulation; most (roughly 70%) relate to employment.
claims.source: US Commission on Civil Rights, "Collateral Consequences: The Crossroads of Punishment, Redemption and the Effects on Communities" (June 2019), citing the NICCC
claims.method: quoted from the report body (extracted text)
claims.notes: Units matter: consequences, not laws. Local ordinances are additional and uncounted.

claims.claim: Among employees who reported misconduct: 79% (US) and a 61% global median said they experienced retaliation (2021 wave); 46% globally in the 2023 wave, consistent with 2020.
claims.units: percent of employees who reported misconduct
claims.source: Ethics & Compliance Initiative, Global Business Ethics Survey, 2021 and 2023 waves
claims.notes: Rates among REPORTERS — misreading them as workforce-wide statistics is the error corrected in commit 2e41a05. 61% is a median across the ten 2021-wave countries.

claims.claim: Share of the world population with access to electricity (most recent year available).
claims.source: World Bank, indicator EG.ELC.ACCS.ZS (World Development Indicators)
claims.notes: Skeleton exemplar of a fetchable entry: value and retrieved are written by the script, never by hand. Run: python3 registry/fetch/worldbank.py EG.ELC.ACCS.ZS WLD --write registry/claims.json --id example-worldbank-electricity-access
